_comment: NIST residential split heat pump, cooling-mode FDD laboratory tests (14 SEER and 16 SEER units, long and short line sets), doi:10.18434/M32132, NIST public-domain data. One worksheet of steady-state test points, one row per averaged test point, grouped by the source file name; the fault levels are in the NF / EF / CF / LL / UC-OC columns. Maps the refrigerant-side and air-side context CAMBER has roles for. subcooling_temp is the liquid-line subcooling at the outdoor unit's liquid service valve (ODLiqSV_Tsub_F), superheat_temp the compressor-suction superheat (CompSuct_Suph_F) and discharge_superheat_temp the compressor discharge superheat (CompDisch_Suph_F), all DIFFERENCES in F computed by the publisher from its R-410A property tables (CAMBER's own R-410A curve reproduces the publisher's saturation temperatures within 0.011 F). The raw line temperatures and pressures behind them are mapped too (liquid_line_temp / liquid_line_pressure at the liquid service valve, suction_line_temp at the vapour service valve, discharge_line_temp at the compressor discharge). suction_pressure is the vapour service valve pressure (1701_ODVapSV_psia), NOT the suction-port column: on the 16 SEER unit 1710_ODSuctPort_psia is a copy of the discharge pressure (see the data issue). The refrigerant pressures are ABSOLUTE (psia) and convert to psig at ingest. return_air_dewpoint_temp is the indoor inlet dew point (chilled-mirror hygrometer), which the indoor-airflow rule needs to match latent load. power is the outdoor unit's (compressor + condenser fan) electrical demand in W. The indoor unit's inlet / exit air-grid temperatures stand in for return / supply air, and 'Indoor Unit SCFM' is the measured indoor airflow at standard density. NOT mapped (no role): capacity, COP, refrigerant mass flow and the other dew points.
